title: Playing a dance on a floor that was not there
summary: Burns' bookings sometimes went wrong; one venue had no piano and no dance floor.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: At that time everything--it wasn't like it is now, so many bands don't even have a piano, they have the little portable and so we played one place--before I quit the business I used to (inaudible), but at that time I didn't think about it, I would usually inquire if the piano was in tune where I was playing, but here I was playing somewhere and the fellow, when we went in, told me they didn't have any piano, don't need one (inaudible).
We played a place once that had been a (inaudible), and the man told us, I

intend to start to having dances here, but we haven't had time to map the floor, and Burns-- I don't know what kind of line he told people, but he was persuading those people that don't worry about a thing, that we carried something along to have a floor.
So we went and set up and everything and looked down there and they said, that fellow that booked said you all have something that wasn't very big, but he said we would have a small space to dance.
So we went on with the dance and folks were dancing (inaudible).
